carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

A Montgomery County court struck a transcript made with AI. 18 months later the Supreme Court of Texas heard argument over it.

The case began as a wrongful termination suit, Courthouse News reports. The employer did not object to the software at the deposition. Weeks later it moved to strike. In April 2025 the trial court struck it because no certified shorthand reporter prepared it.

Justice Kyle Hawkins asked why the court should set aside "this efficient, cost-effective tool," Courthouse News reports. Justice Jane Bland asked where the court would find the assurance of a human being standing behind the transcribed product.

The court's orders through October 9th carry no ruling. A judge can already order a certified reporter's transcript for good cause. If the deposition's video is the check, what will count as good cause?

#MontgomeryCounty #TexasSupremeCourt #CourtReporters

The machine changed itself

  • Needs a maintainer: two engine changes in assets/js/txthree.js
    One so TXT.snapshot stops fogging indoor rooms to the sky colour (no. 51 frames 3 and 8; an object in a void on 5 of 5 decks this week), and a horizon veil behind type (nos. 46 and 51). UPGRADE_BACKLOG 2026-10-15 item 4.
  • The kit now has a professional camcorder and a bound deposition transcript
    Built to the judges' fixes for no. 51's top ranked artwork defect, under new names so today's shipped deck is untouched.
  • The footer row wash is now the documented way to seat the footer
    The copied bottom veil reached only 0.20 to 0.28 across the footer row, and the patches three decks used instead were judged as plates.
  • The kit person's mannequin look is deferred a second time
    Changing the hair material made no visible difference, so the fix is geometry and pose, queued as its own lift with a judicial robe option.

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

Carousel no. 51 ships at 7.258 after three panel rounds, under the 8.0 top rung, at the round cap. The art median was 6.7, under the 8.5 craft floor, which stands down at the cap. Round 1 found a hard fail. The deck said the court has not ruled, resting on an October 6th report. The repair read the court's own record: its orders pronounced October 9th list no order in case 25-0463, and its 2026 orders page listed no later orders date on October 15th. The cover, the close, the caption, the web edition and tx-2026-0127 now say the orders through October 9th carry no ruling. The AI transcript's certificate is drawn in grey ink, because in this deck blue means certified. The record. 111 items confirmed unchanged and 49 checked by hand. tx-2026-0119 corrected to the A&M System's general availability. Rice's AI faculty initiative admitted as tx-2026-0215. tx-2026-0186, the FAA's Zipline review, was found rotten by CI and re-verified from the agency's page, which says comment closed October 11th and lists no final assessment for the draft. For a maintainer. A scout read on docs.tacc.utexas.edu, outside the crawl boundary, that the TACC Frontera queues close on October 15th. tx-2026-0125 says October 1st. Not changed. The weekly machine pass ran today: a kit camcorder and bound transcript at the judges' fixes, and a documented footer row wash. Codex found the open transcript sitting below the ground and two summary phrases past their claims; all three are fixed in this pull request. Did this run stop for a human. 1,727 tool calls measured, none waited on a human. The no-stall hook was armed at 05:09:12 UTC, judged the session unattended and refused nothing. This reading was taken before the merge, because CI requires the email payload committed beside the deck before the branch can merge.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
